findings.body:
**Distinguish unsafe IDs from missing runs.**

The fixture creates only `runs/r1`, and Line 250 accepts the same exception type as the missing-run test. The assertion can pass if an unsafe ID reaches lookup and fails only because there is no usable run there. Assert the invalid-ID diagnostic or verify that lookup never starts.
findings.title: Distinguish unsafe IDs from missing runs.

findings.body:
**Disable signing for fixture commits.**

At Line 868 and Line 947, `--no-verify` does not disable commit signing. If the developer has `commit.gpgSign=true` and no signing key is available, fixture creation fails before source verification runs. Add `--no-gpg-sign` to both commit commands. ([git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit?utm_source=openai))







Also applies to: 947-947
findings.title: Disable signing for fixture commits.

findings.body:
**Supply equal explicit boot IDs in the same-boot case.**

The reboot fixture omits `boot_id_before` and `boot_id_after`. A validator can reject missing IDs but accept equal explicit IDs and still pass this test. Set both fields to `"boot-1"` to test an observed reboot boundary where the boot ID did not change.
findings.title: Supply equal explicit boot IDs in the same-boot case.

findings.body:
**Make the stale digest match the downloaded bytes.**

The downloaded bytes match neither the stale nor the refreshed digest. Checking the wrong manifest therefore still raises `ValueError` and passes this test. Write the actual digest of `b"unexpected"` into the stale manifest, and keep the refreshed digest different. Only verification against the refreshed manifest should then reject the image.
findings.title: Make the stale digest match the downloaded bytes.

findings.body:
**Test each post-boundary refusal independently.**

This test makes activation succeed after both manager restart and reboot. A validator that ignores either boundary still sees the other violation and passes the test. Start from valid boundaries for each case and change one refusal result at a time.







Also applies to: 1691-1692
findings.title: Test each post-boundary refusal independently.

findings.body:
**Check that the images-directory lock is held during the fetch.**

Line 377 checks only the last `flock` call's flag. The test still passes if `fetch_image` takes `LOCK_EX` after `_fetch_image_locked` returns, or takes it on a different file. Check the lock target and acquisition order from the fetch callback so an unprotected fetch fails the test.
findings.title: Check that the images-directory lock is held during the fetch.

findings.body:
**Assert that the required checks are present.**

Line 1327 validates only keys that `build_checks` returns. The test passes if the function omits a required check or returns `{}`. Assert the required keys independently of `build_checks` before checking their values.
findings.title: Assert that the required checks are present.

findings.body:
**Change only the final source manifest in this test.**

The phase dictionaries share one source manifest, and `deepcopy` preserves that sharing within the copy. This assignment changes the prepare manifest as well as the final manifest. A validator that checks only the prepare digest can therefore satisfy the assertion without checking `partial-inspect`. Replace the final `source` dictionary with a copy containing the changed `guest` digest. Leave the other manifests unchanged.
findings.title: Change only the final source manifest in this test.

findings.body:
**Distinguish deferred cleanup from eager calls.**

The AST check accepts both `lambda: stop_process(...)` and a direct `stop_process(...)` call inside a `finish_cleanup` argument. If the direct call raises, Python never enters `finish_cleanup`, so queue and run-metadata restoration can be skipped. Require guarded operations to be inside deferred action bodies, or drive a phase with a mocked stop that raises and assert that restoration still runs.
findings.title: Distinguish deferred cleanup from eager calls.

findings.body:
**Assert that boot-failure cleanup runs under `run.lock`.**

This test checks which stop function ran, but not whether the lock still protected it. If the unguarded stop moved after lock release, every assertion here would still pass, even though another invocation could launch a replacement before the stop. Record lock ownership when the mocked stop runs and assert that the lock is still held.
findings.title: Assert that boot-failure cleanup runs under `run.lock`.

findings.body:
**Build independent before and after snapshots.**

`dict(quiet)` copies only the outer dictionary. When Line 885 changes the after-snapshot timer symlink target, it also changes the before-snapshot target. The test can still pass if the verifier rejects invalid targets but stops detecting target changes between snapshots. Deep-copy `quiet` for the after snapshot so the clean fixture stays equal and one-sided edits affect only one observation.
findings.title: Build independent before and after snapshots.

findings.body:
**Reset the completion baseline for each evidence build.**

`evidence()` stores the generated activation completions back on the test instance. When Line 2788 builds a second fixture in the same test, it starts with the previous fixture's final completions instead of the single seed from `setUp`. Keep the evolving completion list local to `evidence()`. This preserves the append sequence within one fixture and gives each subcase the same starting point.
findings.title: Reset the completion baseline for each evidence build.

findings.body:
**Pass a Git-override-free environment to the fixture Git commands and the CLI child.**

The `git()` helper in `_committed_probe_repo` (line 862) and the `git()` helper in `test_verify_source_scripts_against_a_real_commit` (line 934) call `subprocess.run` without an `env` argument. Setting `cwd` does not remove inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, or `GIT_WORK_TREE`. When a caller sets one of these, `git add .` and `git commit` can act on the caller's index or repository instead of the fixture repository. Run these helpers, and the `subprocess.run` in `_run_probe_cli` (line 874), with one environment that removes Git repository overrides. `_run_probe_cli` also inherits the caller's Git variables.

The impact depends on those variables being set, for example when the suite runs from a Git hook. Ordinary shell runs are not affected.
findings.title: Pass a Git-override-free environment to the fixture Git commands and the CLI child.
